text:
alex chen: Accepted the org invite but I can’t see the private repo redwood-core in the list. I’m listed as a member on the org page though. Tried web + gh CLI. Anyone know who to ping?
onboarding-bot: Welcome to Redwood! If you just joined, some team auto-assignments can take a few minutes. If something seems off, ping #new-hires or people-ops.
alex chen: waited ~15min still nothing. gh shows me as 'Member' but repo access = 404.
maria gonzalez: hi @alex chen — did you accept with your work email (alex@redwood.ai) or personal one?
alex chen: I accepted with alex.chen@gmail.com (I'm switching to work email next). Could that be it?
jamal parker: Alex, that would do it — if your GitHub account email doesn't match the org record, SCIM/team auto-assign can skip you. Can you run `git config --global user.email` and check which email is on your GH account, or just check Settings -> Emails?
alex chen: git says `alex.chen@gmail.com`. my work email is added as secondary on GH but not primary.
jamal parker: Ok. Two quick options:
- change your GH primary email to alex@redwood.ai, or
- org admin can remove and re-invite you using the email on your GH account.
katie (people-ops): I can re-invite using alex.chen@gmail.com if you prefer to keep GH primary. LMK.
alex chen: I'd rather avoid switching right now — please re-invite me to match GH primary.
dev-admin: I resent an invite to alex.chen@gmail.com and manually added you to team eng-core. You should get a new email.
alex chen: got the new invite and accepted it. can see redwood-core now, can clone. thanks!
maria gonzalez: sweet. if anyone else hits this, note: org SCIM/team mappings use the email on the GitHub account. People-ops can re-invite or you can change your GH primary email.
alex chen: tagging this thread: solved :tada:
